en: What's this clod.md file about? It's an
important file you should create in any
Claude Code project you are working on. And
you're also not limited to just one clod.md
file, but I'll get back to that.
Your Claude Code projects should typically
at least have one clod.md file in the root
project folder.
And this file and its content will
automatically be loaded into every new
session you create with Claude Code.
And also if you clear the context of a
session, this file will be loaded into the
newly created context. So what should be in
that file? Well, general rules and general
pieces of information
you
think are relevant to Claude Code. For
example, here, the information that we're
using Bun and that it should
use Bun for executing the scripts in this
project, that is important. And indeed,
there is one change I wanna make here real
quick. In this package.json file
for the dev server and for building and for
start, I'll execute them with this
command here, bun run
--bun to ensure that the Bun runtime gets
used for these commands because that allows
me to then use Bun APIs.
So that's an important piece of information.
We also have some general information about
the architecture in there, but as you see,
it's a rather slim and simple file.
And that's deliberately so because as
mentioned, this will be included in every
prompt and therefore it shouldn't be super
large because you'll just pollute your
context if you have a lot of information in
there.
There are a couple of tweaks I wanna make
though. For example, I'll add,
we're building the app described in
@spec.md to point at this spec.md file,
which of course includes a more detailed
description of the app we're building. And
to ensure that Claude will not always read
that file, which is rather large, I'll give
it some hint on when it might want to look
at this spec.md file, specifically here when
tackling general architectural tasks
or to double-check the database structure,
tech stack, or just application architecture
as a whole.
I also have one other instruction I
typically like to include here. I want
Claude Code to give me short replies, no
long essays with lots of
code snippets in there because all that will
be tokens I'm paying for and all that will
be tokens that pollute the context as a
conversation goes on for longer. So that's
one additional instruction I like to have in
my Claude MD files.
And then there are more tweaks we'll make
throughout this project. But for now, that's
it. Now I did mention that you can have
multiple Claude.md files in your project.
And you can indeed add as many as you want
by simply putting them into subfolders. The
important thing there will just be that
those nested clod.md files will only be read
and loaded by Claude when it works on files
in that subfolder. So if I added a clod.md
file here in the app folder,
the content of this file, this clod.md file,
will be loaded and considered whenever
Claude does work on any file in the app
folder, which for this project would very
often be the case since a lot of our code
will go in there.
But you get the point and you can have as
many levels of nesting of nesting as you
want and then add your folder-specific
Claude.md files as needed.
The core purpose of this Claude.md file
therefore simply is to store some long-term
memory that should be accessible across
different sessions and about having those
core
instructions that will apply to essentially
every prompt.
